tools.name: figma_execute_code
tools.description: WRITE tool: run JavaScript in the open Figma document (Figma Desktop + 'Mokido' plugin) to create, edit, move, style or delete nodes. To READ (explore a section, list children, find layers, check texts / fonts / variants / table columns) call figma_inspect instead: every id in one call, one line per node, view:"table" for tables; a read script here costs a model turn per question and its reply names the figma_inspect call to use (use_instead). Every call is a full model turn, so make the whole change in ONE call — all screens / breakpoints, verified in the same code with bridge.check — and put capture_node_ids on that same call instead of a separate figma_screenshot. Globals: `figma`, `await ensureFont(family, style)`, `getFreePosition(w, h)`, `bridge`: bridge.check({ '1:2': { width: 320, fill: '#FFFFFF' } }) -> pass/fail list; bridge.define(name, src) + bridge.require(name) keep helpers between calls (each call is a fresh function body — never eval); `return bridge.info()` lists the rest. Macros: bridge.replaceWithInstance(target, comp, {props, text}), bridge.setProps(inst, {Status: 'Dropdown'}), bridge.setText(root, {layer: '…'}) or bridge.setText(textNode, 'new text') (keeps mixed font styles, sizes, colours by words: THE way to replace the text of a label with several font styles — never `characters =`, which flattens them, and never a per-character getRangeFontName/setRangeFontName loop), bridge.shift(ids, {dx, dy}), bridge.moveInto(ids, section, {layout, gap}), bridge.fitSection(s), bridge.context(id), bridge.componentize(nodeObject) -> new COMPONENT, same name/size/look, NEW id (never raw createComponentFromNode), prototype links: await bridge.openOverlay(triggerId, overlayFrameId, { position: 'BOTTOM_CENTER', dim: 0.4, closeOnOutside: true }) (the overlay look is read-only in the Plugin API: the reply names the MANUAL STEP for the user), bridge.closeOverlay(id), bridge.setReaction(id, { to: frameId, nav: 'NAVIGATE' }); read links with figma_inspect view:"flow". Call macros directly, don't read their source. Never findAll the whole page — scope to a section. Return only the ids/flags you need: responses over max_output_bytes (3500) are shrunk, the full value stays in bridge.state.lastResult.

code.description: JavaScript to run in the Figma sandbox, compiled as an async function body (top-level await and return allowed; import/export are not). Example: const frame = figma.createFrame(); frame.resize(400, 600); frame.name = 'Card'; figma.currentPage.appendChild(frame); return 'Created frame';

description.description: Short human-readable description of the action (e.g. 'Create login modal', 'Update brand colors') shown in Figma toasts and logs.

capture.description: Set to true to capture a PNG of what this call created/modified and return it for visual verification. Never touches the user's selection — see capture_node_ids.

capture_node_ids.description: Node ids to screenshot instead of the default (whatever this call created/modified, falling back to the user's current selection only if neither exists). The user's selection is never mutated to enable a capture.

diff.description: Currently ignored (the "before" screenshot stalls the plugin); the reply has the after image only.

max_px.description: Longest side of each returned image in px (default: 1024). Image tokens grow with pixel count, not file size.

max_output_bytes.description: Cap on the whole text response in UTF-8 bytes (default: 3500 — under the ~4 KB at which some clients spill output to a file and cost an extra turn; in clients that spill big outputs to a file, 0 and values above 3900 become 3900). Larger results are shrunk structurally (multi-line text is cut by whole lines), cuts marked with ….

async.description: Return { status: 'running', job_id } immediately instead of waiting — collect it later with figma_job_status. Calls that run past 45s do this automatically.

target.description: fileName of a specific connected Figma document to run this in, when more than one is open (see figma_list_targets). Defaults to whichever is currently focused.

tools.name: figma_inspect
tools.description: READ the live Figma document in ONE call — the tool for any read (not figma_execute_code); pass every node id you need at once instead of one call per node. Default: a compact outline, one line per node (TYPE "name" #id WxH @x,y [V gap8 pad16 fill/hug a:start/center] size:fill/hug fill:#FFF stroke:#E8EAF0/0,1,1,1 r0,0,3,3 shadow:… font "text…"; non-defaults only; a TEXT named after its text drops the name; `a:P/C` = primaryAxisAlignItems/counterAxisAlignItems, start = MIN, center = CENTER, end = MAX, between = SPACE_BETWEEN, absent = MIN/MIN), as deep as fits the reply unless `depth` is given; `children:N` marks a node with more below. `like: "<ref id>"` (or several) FINDS every copy of the reference under node_ids (screens/sections; default: its section) — instances of the same component, or same name — and diffs each against it: the call for "redo these like the reference" when you don't know where the copies are. `compare: "<ref id>"` lists, per node_id, every difference from that reference (layout, sizing, stroke, radius, effects, clip, font, variant; children matched by name) and ends with REF lines, the reference's exact values to copy into the write (no props read needed) — one call for "make these like that one", and the check after the write. `props` returns exact values instead: { id: { prop: value } } (also fill, stroke, text, font, layout, padding, parent, children, main, variant, props, absolute, reactions, connector). `find` searches node names under node_ids (or the current page); `find_text` searches text content. `view: "map"` = canvas map (sections, breakpoints). `view: "flow"` = the prototype links under node_ids (a section or screens): per screen, source, trigger, action, target, transition, plus the overlay settings of overlay targets — never scan the page for `reactions`. `context: true` adds ancestor sections, breakpoints and component variants. `offset` skips the first N outline lines when a reply ends with `pass offset=K`. `check` returns only mismatches. Combine them freely. Changes nothing.

node_ids.description: Node ids to read ("12:34" or "12-34"). Omit to use the current page.

node_id.description: Alias of node_ids for one id.

depth.description: Outline levels below each node (0 = the nodes only, max 6). Omit it: the outline goes as deep as fits the reply.

props.description: Return these properties per node instead of an outline, e.g. ["width", "layoutSizingHorizontal", "fill", "text"]; also "reactions" (prototype interactions), "connector" (FigJam connector ends) and "texts" (all texts below a frame, id + full characters, pages with offset).

view.description: "outline" (default) = one line per node; "map" = canvas map: sections, frames, breakpoints and component sets in a few lines; "table" = per table (found by structure) the columns: header, width, sizing, cell contents, plus row and cell ids; "flow" = prototype links (screen, source, trigger, action, target, transition, overlay settings) under node_ids (without node_ids: every top-level screen of the current page).

context.description: Also return, per node: ancestor sections, breakpoint siblings and component variants ({ id: context }).

like.description: Reference node id (several: comma-separated): find its copies under node_ids (default: the reference's top section) and list, per copy, its frame and how it differs (missing children come with the reference's own line, and REF lines at the end give the reference's exact values, so no extra read is needed). Copies that already match are listed as identical.

compare.description: Reference node id: instead of an outline, list how each node_id differs from it (x/y/width and text content are skipped; height, stroke sides/align are compared). Ends with REF lines: the exact values of the differing reference nodes, to copy in figma_execute_code without a props read. 'identical' = nothing to fix.

find_text.description: Case-insensitive substring of TEXT content to search for under node_ids (or the current page). One line per match: #id "layer" «text» in <parent layer #id>, screen "<top frame>" (the parent is the frame to click or edit).

offset.description: Skip the first N lines of the outline / found list (use the K from a '… pass offset=K' line to read the next page).

find.description: Case-insensitive substring of node names to search for under node_ids (or the current page). Up to 8 matches come back with their subtree outline (as deep as fits, no extra read needed); more matches as one line each.

find_type.description: Restrict find to one node type, e.g. FRAME, TEXT, INSTANCE.

check.description: Expectations to verify: { "12:34": { "width": 320, "fill": "#FFFFFF", "layout": "V gap8 pad16" } }. Returns { pass, fail: [{ id, key, want, got }], missing }.

max_output_bytes.description: Cap on the text response in UTF-8 bytes (default 3500; in clients that spill big outputs to a file, 0 and values above 3900 become 3900). A cut outline ends with '… pass offset=K': use `offset` to page instead of raising this.

target.description: fileName of a specific connected Figma document, when more than one is open (see figma_list_targets).

tools.name: figma_html
tools.description: WRITE tool: build a screen from ONE HTML (flex -> Auto Layout, text, fills, borders, shadows, svg). Pass `html` or `path` of a local .html (no JS, <style> inside, Inter, flex+gap not margin, data-name = layer name; else warnings). Reply: root ids, layers, auto_layout share, absolute_fallback, text_wrapped (extra line wraps, want 0), boxes_within_1px, <=10 warnings. widths:[1440,390] = one frame per width. Plugin window must be open.

html.description: Full HTML document or fragment. Use `path` instead for big pages.

path.description: Absolute or relative path of a local .html file on this machine (read by the server, up to 2 MB). Give either html or path.

width.description: Viewport width in px the HTML is laid out at (default 1440, 100..8000). Media queries use it.

widths.description: Several viewport widths, e.g. [1440, 390]: one frame per width, placed side by side. Overrides width.

height.description: Viewport height in px for 100vh rules (default 900). The frame is as tall as the page.

name.description: Name of the root frame (default 'HTML'; with widths the width is appended).

parent.description: Id of a frame or section to build into (default: free space on the current page).

x.description: Canvas x of the root (default: free space).

y.description: Canvas y of the root (default: free space).

capture.description: Also return a PNG of the built frame.

max_output_bytes.description: Cap on the text response in UTF-8 bytes (default 3500).

target.description: fileName of a specific connected Figma document when more than one is open (see figma_list_targets).

tools.name: figma_screenshot
tools.description: Capture PNG screenshots of specific nodes or the current selection in Figma, to check layout, contrast, typography and spacing. Each image costs ~1k tokens at the default max_px, and stays in context: check mechanical things through write-call `warnings` or bridge.check first, and take one screenshot per finished stage rather than after every edit. Right after a figma_execute_code edit, put capture_node_ids on that call instead — this tool is then an extra turn.

node_ids.description: Optional comma-separated list of Figma node IDs to screenshot (e.g. '123:456, 123:457'). If omitted, captures current selection or entire page.

max_px.description: Longest side of each image in px (default: 1024). Raise only to read fine detail; crop with node_ids instead where possible.

description.description: Optional action description for Figma toast and logs.

target.description: fileName of a specific connected Figma document, when more than one is open (see figma_list_targets).

tools.name: figma_get_selection
tools.description: Get information and properties (dimensions, coordinates, text, fills, parent, page, AutoLayout context) of the currently selected nodes on the Figma canvas.

target.description: fileName of a specific connected Figma document, when more than one is open (see figma_list_targets).

tools.name: figma_find_components
tools.description: Find and inspect components, component sets, variants, and component property definitions in the active Figma file without flooding LLM context. Returns names, variant values, keys, and IDs.

query.description: Search query to filter components by name, description, or variant name (optional, if empty returns all top components)

page_name.description: Optional page name filter (e.g. '🎨 Design System' or 'Components')

include_variants.description: Whether to collect and return all available variant property keys and values (default: true)

limit.description: Maximum number of components to return to prevent token bloat (default: 30)

refresh_index.description: Force a fresh scan instead of using the cached component index (normally at most 60s stale — see figma_read_canvas / instructions for how the index works).

target.description: fileName of a specific connected Figma document, when more than one is open (see figma_list_targets).

tools.name: figma_insert_component_instance
tools.description: Create and insert an instance of a master component or component set into the canvas or target AutoLayout container. Supports selecting variants, applying text overrides with auto font loading, and can return a PNG screenshot (capture: true) for visual verification.

component_name.description: Name of the master component or ComponentSet to instantiate (e.g. 'Button', 'Card', 'Input')

component_id.description: Direct node ID of the master component or ComponentSet (optional alternative to component_name)

properties.description: Key-value map of variant properties and component properties to apply (e.g. {'Type': 'Primary', 'Size': 'MD', 'State': 'Default'})

text_overrides.description: Key-value map of text overrides for text layers inside the component (e.g. {'Label': 'Submit', 'Description': 'Confirm order'})

target_parent_id.description: Target container/frame node ID to insert the instance into. If omitted, inserts into current selected frame or active page.

position.description: Optional placement coordinates or child index in AutoLayout container

capture.description: Whether to capture and return a PNG screenshot of the inserted instance (default: false)

target.description: fileName of a specific connected Figma document, when more than one is open (see figma_list_targets).

tools.name: figma_get_variables
tools.description: Retrieve all Figma Variable collections, modes (e.g. Light/Dark), and design tokens (colors, numbers, strings, booleans) from the active document.

collection_name.description: Optional filter by variable collection name (e.g. 'Theme', 'Tokens', 'Spacing')

limit.description: Maximum number of tokens to return across all matched collections, to prevent token bloat on large design-token files (default: 300)

target.description: fileName of a specific connected Figma document, when more than one is open (see figma_list_targets).

tools.name: figma_set_variables_mode
tools.description: Switch the active Figma Variables mode (e.g. Dark Mode, Light Mode, Brand theme) for a specific artboard/frame or the entire page.

target_id.description: Target node ID (frame/artboard) to set mode on. If omitted, applies to current selection or active page.

capture.description: Whether to capture a PNG screenshot of the target after switching mode (default: false)

target.description: fileName of a specific connected Figma document, when more than one is open (see figma_list_targets).

tools.name: figma_insert_svg
tools.description: Insert raw SVG/vector code directly into Figma canvas or target AutoLayout container with automatic scale-proportional resizing, fill/stroke color overrides, optional component creation, and an optional PNG screenshot (capture: true).

name.description: Optional layer name for the created SVG node (e.g. 'Icon / Shield', 'Brand / Google')

fill_override.description: Specific fill color override (Hex e.g. '#FFFFFF' or RGB) applied to vector shapes with non-empty fills

stroke_override.description: Specific stroke color override (Hex e.g. '#6366F1' or RGB) applied to vector paths with non-empty strokes

color_override.description: Universal color override (Hex '#6366F1' or RGB) applied to all active fills and strokes

target_parent_id.description: Target container/frame node ID to insert the SVG into. If omitted, inserts into current selected frame or active page.

position.description: Optional placement coordinates or child index in AutoLayout container

as_component.description: Whether to wrap the resulting SVG node into a reusable master ComponentNode (default: false)

capture.description: Whether to capture and return a PNG screenshot of the inserted SVG (default: false)

target.description: fileName of a specific connected Figma document, when more than one is open (see figma_list_targets).

tools.name: figma_get_canvas_layout
tools.description: Inspect top-level frames and artboards on the active Figma page to prevent overlap. Returns all screen coordinates, bounding box, and a calculated 'suggestedNextPosition' for placing new artboards safely.

direction.description: Placement direction relative to existing screens ('RIGHT' or 'BOTTOM', default: 'RIGHT')

limit.description: Maximum number of artboards to list, to prevent token bloat on pages with hundreds of frames (default: 200)

layout.description: 'row' (default) places along one axis per `direction`, like before. 'grid' shelf-packs into a `columns`-wide grid so a run of generated screens fills a compact rectangle instead of one long ribbon.

target.description: fileName of a specific connected Figma document, when more than one is open (see figma_list_targets).

tools.name: figma_rollback
tools.description: Undo what a previous write call (figma_execute_code, figma_insert_component_instance, figma_insert_svg) did: removes nodes it created and restores properties on nodes it modified. Deletions the code performed on pre-existing nodes are never recoverable. Every write call's response includes the checkpoint_id to pass here.

checkpoint_id.description: The checkpoint_id from a previous write call's response. Omit (or pass "last") to roll back the most recent not-yet-rolled-back checkpoint.

target.description: fileName of a specific connected Figma document, when more than one is open (see figma_list_targets).

tools.name: figma_job_status
tools.description: Wait for a figma_execute_code call that came back as { status: 'running', job_id } (it ran past 45s, or was called with async: true). BLOCKS until the job finishes or wait_ms passes, then returns the same result/screenshot the synchronous call would have — so call it once, not in a polling loop. `stalled: true` means the plugin looks frozen: STOP, ask the user to check Figma; a second figma_job_status for that job returns at once with the same advice. A finished job is forgotten after being read once.

job_id.description: The job_id from figma_execute_code's { status: 'running', job_id } response.

wait_ms.description: How long to block waiting for the job to finish (default: 45000, max: 55000; 0 = just peek).

tools.name: figma_list_targets
tools.description: List every Figma document currently connected to this bridge (fileName, current page, which one is focused). Use this when a LIVE tool call fails with AMBIGUOUS_TARGET, or before working with a specific file among several open at once — pass the fileName as `target` on any LIVE tool.

tools.name: figma_read_canvas
tools.description: Read the LIVE, currently-open Figma document as token-optimized Pseudo-JSX/Tree/JSON — the same pipeline get_file/get_node use for the cloud API, applied to whatever is open in Figma Desktop right now. Prefer this over hand-writing a tree walk in figma_execute_code; it is far cheaper in tokens and its output format matches get_file/get_node exactly.

node_ids.description: Comma-separated node IDs to read. Omit to read the top-level frames of the current page.

format.description: Output format — same meaning as get_file/get_node (default: 'jsx').

depth.description: Traversal depth from each requested node, hard-capped at 12 (default: 6).

include_hidden.description: Whether to include hidden (visible=false) layers (default: false).

budget_tokens.description: Target response size in tokens (default: 4000). If the requested depth overshoots this, depth is reduced and re-serialized (no extra round trip) until it fits, with a trailing comment noting the reduction.

target.description: fileName of a specific connected Figma document, when more than one is open (see figma_list_targets).
